builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
summary: The method replaces manual, expert-driven kernel development for poorly documented or new AI accelerators. It costs significant LLM inference, multi-day device time on scarce hardware, and the operational complexity of maintaining an agent loop that builds and revalidates its own target knowledge. It can fail if the agent generates incorrect or illegal kernels that pass screening but degrade performance, or if toolchain changes invalidate accumulated knowledge without detection.
rationale: The reader operates under constrained infrastructure and lacks access to scarce, specialized accelerators or the multi-day device time required; the technique is relevant but impractical to adopt without those resources.
technique: Multi-agent LLM loop for kernel optimization on novel accelerators

claims.statement: The method replaces manual, expert-driven kernel development for poorly documented or new AI accelerators. It costs significant LLM inference, multi-day device time on scarce hardware, and the operational complexity of maintaining an agent loop that builds and revalidates its own target knowledge. It can fail if the agent generates incorrect or illegal kernels that pass screening but degrade performance, or if toolchain changes invalidate accumulated knowledge without detection.
The final kernels reach a 9.293x geomean speedup over the official baseline, each within 1.25x of the cycles needed just to move its weights.
